People development approach

On the basis of two core values - humanity and responsibility, GREENFEED is striving to build a good working environment where every individual
is trained and developed (Grow Talents), is taken care of (Grow Care) in order to bring quality products and services to customers, consumers,
and spread more goodness to the community (Grow Impact).
At GREENFEED, people are our utmost important asset. We are committed to growing our workforce, creating a healthy and inspiring work environment on the foundation of caring, shared goodness, and sustainable culture.

GREENFEED employees are guided to act according to five management and leadership competencies, which are:

  • 1 Result orientation
  • 2 Self- and organization-growth vision
  • 3 Connective leadership
  • 4 Team building and development
  • 5 Innovation and future-oriented
    leadership

Training and talent development

In 2022, GREENFEED established a training program for 22 high-level leaders who make a significant impact on stakeholders engagement and business strategy. It also conducted employee performance appraisals to identify personnel who are capable of rising through the ranks and joining training programs for successors.

As contribution to sustainable workforce for Agriculture sector, GREENFEED has collaborated with universities and educational organizations to promote talent programs. In 2022, the Group conducted training activities for 133 second and third-year students, issued certificates for 109 students participating in "Seeds of Talents" program.

Reasonable remuneration policy

In 2022, GREENFEED launched GREENCARE program with a focus on physical and mental healthcare for employees. Meanwhile, the Outrace
club was kicked off to encourage employees to become involved in physical activities such as running, swimming, yoga, and cycling.
The club also supports members to register for sport events such as VnExpress Marathon, helping employees to regain positive energy
and improve work-life balance.

Occupational safety
management approach

For jobs involving a high degree of risk,
the Group provides detailed instruction
on how to use personal protective
equipment, and deal with dangerous
situations. It is vital to help
employees identify deficiencies,
assess their effect, and take
corrective actions. Safety culture
is also considered as top priority
in manufacturing and business operation.

Programs to promote a safety
culture at GREENFEED:

  • Organizing periodic EHS assessments to encourage good practices and improve working conditions

  • Offering safety training and issuing annual certifications to employees

  • Conducting internal safety training twice a year, led by EHS specialists.

  • Implementing biannual health examinations and monitoring for positions involving heavy work and exposure to hazardous factors

  • Reviewing emergency response and fire prevention plans

Strategic approach to corporate social responsibility

GREENFEED develops corporate social responsibility programs based on a comprehensive assessment of their long term impact on society. Our programs
focus on supporting women, children and local communities with involvement and consultation of local government agencies, associations, and social
organizations.

Enhancing children’s nutrition

Remarkable achievements up to 2022

Elevating women’s livelihoods

Kicked off in 2010, Empowering Farmers program of GREENFEED, collaborated with Farmers' Associations in various provinces and Tuoi Tre newspaper, has accompanied thousands of farmers, especially rural women to elevate their livelihoods through financial support and training in animal husbandry.
In 2022, GREENFEED continued to launch the Sharing Wealth with Farmers program with a focus on planting practices, offering farmers new opportunities to uplift their livelihoods.

PERIODICALLY PROVIDE NUTRITIOUS MEALS

In 2022, there were 10 shelters and 1 school added to the list of recipients to receive periodic food support from the program.

SCALE UP SUPPORT THROUGH MEANINGFUL ACTIVITIES

In addition to periodic support, the program also presented food products and organized engaging activities for children on special occasions.
